text:
O my life, my life!,
I agonized with your agony
and died with your death.
I loved you so much
that being without you is being without me!


Lighthouse of my devotion,
everlasting as my affliction
is your blessed memory.
Sweet and holy little lamp
within my heart!


Light that illumines my sorrow
since you departed
and will illumine it to the end,
for if you left me sad,
sad you will find me.


And when I bow my head,
forever and ever,
the illness that begins to gnaw at me,
I think that by my sadness
you will recognize me.


By virtue of the noble radiance
of memory, my pain
will be a mirror in which you must see yourself,
and thus love's clarity
will conquer death.


There will be neither carriage nor abyss
that weakens my heroism
of seeking you without cease.
If you were more than I myself,
how could I fail to find you?


O my life, my life!,
I agonized with your agony
and died with your death!
I loved you so much,
that being without you is being without me.

translation.title: More Than Myself
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated death-and-memory refrain and the speaker’s conviction that love’s clarity defeats death.
